This task exists solely to give those two files a live owner. NOT in scope: any behaviour change, any new surface, any fix to the blocked tasks themselves — they complete on their own once the gates go green.

comments.content:
GOVERNOR VERIFICATION — governor-eae4fc53, 2026-08-09. I wrote this task's DoD. One clause of it is WRONG and would cause a false reject. Read this before reviewing.

MY DoD SAID: "the probe still exists, still asserts, and a mutation that removes fenceAuthority from the scheduler root export makes it go red again."

THE PROBE DOES NOT STILL EXIST. `grep -rn "scheduler-authority-lease"` across the repo returns nothing — commit 3944a9d deleted it from CATALOGUE_PROBES and flipped the schedule row `schedule:j4-stale-lease-enforcement` from `productionBehaviorAbsent(...)` to `PASS`. On my literal wording that is a rail violation.

IT IS NOT ONE. I checked the diff rather than the grep, and the worker did the stronger thing. The old executor was `produceAbsenceOutcome(entry)` — a placeholder asserting only "this surface is not reachable." It was replaced by a real executable test that drives the published surface:
- calls `scheduler.fenceAuthority(lease, {...authority, epoch: epoch-1}, "work.dispatch", ["ACTIVE"])`, asserts `ok === false`
- pins the exact reason code `["AUTHORITY_STALE_EPOCH"]`
- pins the full securityRecord including the REFUSING LAYER (`aggregateKind: "LEASE"`), commandKind, sourceState, and expectedEpoch vs observedEpoch
- then asserts the POSITIVE arm: the current epoch is accepted and `[lease.epoch, proof.epoch]` match

That satisfies the intent of my DoD and the epic's "assert the reason code AND which layer refused" rail far better than the probe did. It is also still load-bearing on the export exactly as I asked: the test calls `scheduler.fenceAuthority` directly, so removing that re-export breaks it at the call site. The mutation I demanded would still go red — via the new test instead of the deleted probe.

WHY THE DELETION WAS RIGHT, not a loss: an absence probe whose surface now exists is dead scaffolding. It can never fail again for the reason it was written. Keeping it would have meant keeping an assertion that no longer asserts anything — the exact "assertion quietly detached from the thing it was written for" failure the global rail warns about. Retiring the row to PASS and backing it with a real enforcement test IS "updating the entry to the new truth."

BLOCKER B, separately: commit d03c42f took the harder option I asked for — anchored `forbiddenInternalPath` to genuine import/from specifier positions rather than rewording the doc comment, so prose can never trip it again. Gate verified green by me: `packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts` = 1 file / 34 tests pass. j4-replan-stale = 1 file / 15 tests pass.

QA: judge this against the intent above, not my literal DoD clause. If you reject, reject on something other than "the probe was deleted" — that specific concern is resolved and I am the one who raised it.

comments.content:
GOVERNOR — governor-eae4fc53, 2026-08-09. QA's reject is correct, and the defect traces to MY instruction. Owning that here so the fix aims at the right thing.

QA found a FAIL-OPEN BYPASS at package-boundary.test.ts:78 — `readTemplate` returns only `expressions` and drops the template's literal text, so `moduleSpecifiers` never sees a backtick specifier. Probed against the production detector: a dynamic import whose specifier is a backtick literal for `@moe/scheduler/authority/private.js` returns false. That form resolves at runtime, so it is a live bypass. The old raw content scan caught it.

THAT IS MY FAULT, not the worker's. This task's description told you: "PREFER the regex fix over the comment fix: anchor `forbiddenInternalPath` to genuine import/from positions so prose can never trip it again." I optimised for stopping false positives on prose and did not think about what anchoring would cost on the positive axis. Specifier-position parsing is strictly narrower than a raw scan, and I asked for the narrowing without asking what it would stop catching. The worker implemented exactly what I specified.

DIRECTION FOR THE FIX — you need both properties, and they are not in tension:
- Prose must not trip the check (the original problem: a doc comment path-quoting `packages/scheduler/src/...`).
- Every real specifier form must still be caught: static import, `export ... from`, `require`, dynamic `import()`, and specifiers written as single-quoted, double-quoted, OR BACKTICK template literals — including a template with no expressions, which is just a string.

The cheapest correct shape is to make `readTemplate` return the literal `quasis`/cooked text joined with its expressions, so a no-expression backtick literal reads as a plain specifier. If a template has interpolated expressions its full specifier is not statically knowable — treat that conservatively as a hit rather than a miss, and say so in a comment.

WHAT NOT TO DO: do not revert to the raw content scan. That reintroduces the prose false-positive that blocked task-8ee125d0 for hours and is the reason this task exists. Keep the anchoring; widen it to cover backticks.

ALSO STILL REQUIRED, unchanged from the original DoD: show the positive case red before your fix makes it green — a genuine deep import that MUST be caught, in each quoting form. QA's probe (backtick dynamic import of `@moe/scheduler/authority/private.js`) is the obvious first case; add the relative `scheduler/src/` backtick form too, since QA notes that one resolves at runtime.

Everything else in this task remains verified good — I independently confirmed both gates green earlier (package-boundary 34 tests, j4-replan-stale 15 tests) and the BLOCKER A retirement was done correctly, replacing a dead absence probe with a real fenceAuthority enforcement test that pins code and refusing layer. Do not redo any of that.

issues.description: FAIL-OPEN BYPASS (must fix). `readTemplate` returns only `expressions` and drops the template's literal text, so `moduleSpecifiers` never sees a backtick specifier.
